## Document Metadata
- **Type:** Statement of Work (SOW) / Proposal
- **Client/Agency:** U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) Volcano Hazards Program
- **Program/Solicitation:** USGS Purchase Request; NASA Phase II-E SBIR (mentioned for co-funding)
- **Date:** 26 July 2019
- **BST Products/Systems Referenced:** S2 UAS
- **Key Personnel:** Jack Elston (last editor); USGS contacts: Angie Diefenbach, Christoph Kern

## Executive Summary
This SOW outlines Black Swift Technologies' proposed development and deployment of a specialized payload for the S2 UAS to conduct volcano monitoring missions for the USGS. The payload would integrate multiple gas sensors, spectroscopy equipment, and imaging systems to characterize volcanic emissions and topography from a safe distance of 10-15 km. BST would design the payload, develop real-time telemetry systems, conduct validation flights, and deploy the system to Makushin Volcano in Alaska for operational monitoring.

## Technical Approach

### Payload Development & Integration
- Design one or two nosecones for the S2 UAS capable of housing specialized sensors
- Identify communication interfaces, power requirements, and weight/volume optimization for each sensor
- Develop data recording system with geographic and temporal tagging for post-processing
- Create calibration procedures and pre/post-flight protocols in collaboration with USGS
- Conduct bench testing and characterization of sensor rise time and critical properties
- Perform local validation flights (near BST headquarters in Colorado) to verify performance during flight

### Telemetry & Ground Systems
- Develop high-data-rate, long-distance real-time telemetry system for video and sensor streams
- Create improved base-station display software capable of:
  - Displaying video alongside real-time sensor data
  - Color-coded flight route visualization
  - Real-time spectroscopic analysis of UV spectral data

### Regulatory & Operational
- Secure necessary FAA flight permissions and operational authority
- Provide documentation for future USGS and Department of Interior Office of Aviation Services approval
- Plan mission series with USGS and handle logistics
- Conduct flight operations with NASA staff assuming Operational Control
- Coordinate with USGS scientists and NASA observers on-site

## Products & Capabilities Described

### S2 UAS
- **What it is:** Black Swift's intermediate-range unmanned aircraft system
- **Proposed use:** Volcano monitoring platform with 10-15 km range capability, capable of climbing to 10,000-15,000 feet summit elevations
- **Enhancement:** Development of "more robust S2 platform for low-temperature environments available to procure"

### Payload Sensor Suite
Nosecone(s) integrating:
- **Gas sensors:** CO2, SO2, H2S concentration measurement
- **Spectroscopy:** Upward-looking UV spectrometer measuring scattered sunlight radiance to determine vertical column SO2 (used to calculate total SO2 emission rates)
- **Environmental sensors:** 3D wind velocity, temperature, relative humidity, pressure
- **Positioning & Imaging:** GPS with real-time kinematic (RTK) geotagging capability
- **Camera systems:** Nadir photogrammetry camera for digital elevation models and deformation detection; gimbaled or forward-looking video camera for observations

## Use Cases & Applications

### Primary Mission: Volcano Gas Emissions Monitoring
- **Objective:** Characterize gas composition and emission rates during volcanic activity
- **Measurements:** Relative abundances of H2O, CO2, SO2, H2S; total SO2 emission rates; emission rates of all primary volatile species
- **Advantage over manned operations:** Eliminates need for costly helicopter support and allows safe observation from 10-15 km distance

### Secondary Mission: Topographic & Deformation Monitoring
- High-resolution baseline topographic models via photogrammetry
- Repeat surveys to characterize deformation rates, volumes, and extents of lava emissions
- Detection of subsurface magma presence indicators

### Target Volcano: Makushin, Alaska
- **Location:** Northern end of Unalaska Island, eastern Aleutians; 25 km west of Dutch Harbor
- **Characteristics:** Active volcano, rated "Very High Threat" in National Volcano Early Warning System (NVEWS)
- **Justification:** 
  - 2018 gas survey showed hundreds of tons SO2 per day emissions (indicating shallow magma)
  - Follow-up survey planned for summer 2019 but restricted by helicopter availability
  - Summit elevation 1800 m accessible via intermediate-range UAS
  - Close proximity to Dutch Harbor (accessible via commercial flights)
  - Archetype for revolutionizing USGS volcano monitoring capability
  - Baseline monitoring possible at least once per year

## Key Deliverables

1. **Customized nosecone(s)** with integrated gas sensors (CO2, SO2, H2S), UV spectrometer, 3D wind sensor, environmental sensors, RTK-enabled photogrammetry camera, and video camera
2. **Enhanced S2 UAS platform** optimized for low-temperature environments
3. **High-data-rate long-distance telemetry system** with real-time video streaming capability
4. **Base-station display software** with video overlay, real-time sensor data visualization, flight route mapping, and spectroscopic analysis
5. **Bench test and validation flight data** (Colorado-based testing) with documentation
6. **Mission deployment data** from target volcano operations
7. **Final reports** documenting deployment activities and aircraft characteristics for future DOI Office of Aviation Services procurement/approval

## Notable Details

### Operational Model
- BST responsible for all flight operations logistics and data collection
- NASA personnel assume Operational Control of aircraft during flights
- USGS scientists and NASA observers present on-site during operations
- Period of Performance: September 1, 2019 – August 31, 2020
- Two-week deployment to Makushin Volcano planned

### Budget & Funding
- USGS provided budget: $99,925 (core payload development and 2-week deployment)
- NASA Phase II-E SBIR funding to cover additional development (Part II budget shown separately for informational purposes)

### Intellectual Property & Data Ownership
- **USGS owns:** All data, nosecone sensors, and documents produced under this SOW
- **BST restrictions:** Cannot utilize or share any data products without explicit written USGS permission
- **USGS flexibility:** Reserves right to utilize, revise, modify, or have documents modified by others as deemed necessary

### Regulatory Considerations
- Flight permission acquisition and documentation needed for future Department of Interior Office of Aviation Services approval
- Alternative target volcano selection possible if permitting or volcanic activity forecasting creates uncertainties
- Detailed aircraft and flight characteristics documentation required for future government procurement

### Competitive Advantage Highlighted
- Intermediate-range capability (10-15 km) exceeds typical commercial sUAS limitations
- Enables safe observation of explosive, unpredictable volcanoes during active phases
- Eliminates need for close-range operations in hazardous environments
- Real-time telemetry and decision-making capability during observation missions
- Integrated multi-parameter monitoring (gas composition + topography) in single platform# BlackSwift-USC Proposal for Soil Moisture In-Situ Data Products

## Document Metadata
- Type: Subcontract Proposal / Statement of Work
- Client/Agency: Black Swift Technologies (BST); University of Southern California (USC)
- Program/Solicitation: NASA SBIR Phase II (Soil Moisture topic)
- Date: May 12-14, 2015
- BST Products/Systems Referenced: L-band radiometer mounted on Uninhabited Aerial System (UAS)
- Key Personnel: Dr. Maciej Stachura (BST), Mahta Moghaddam (USC PI), Ben Holstein (USC Contracts & Grants)

## Executive Summary
USC proposes to support Black Swift Technologies' NASA SBIR Phase II project by providing in-situ soil moisture measurements from the SoilSCAPE wireless sensor network during flight testing of BST's L-band radiometer on a UAS near Canton, Oklahoma. USC will maintain, calibrate, and operate 10-20 soil moisture sensor nodes to provide ground-truth validation data for the radiometer system over a one-month period (May 15 - June 14, 2015).

## Technical Approach
- Deploy and operate the SoilSCAPE wireless sensor network (previously developed under NASA funding) at a 300m × 300m test field near Canton, Oklahoma
- Provide in-situ soil moisture measurements at three depths: ~5 cm, ~10 cm, and ~30 cm
- Install sensors at 10-20 locations across the field
- Conduct pre-flight field visits to ensure all wireless sensor network nodes are operational and producing quality data
- Perform maintenance and repairs on sensor nodes as needed
- Transmit real-time data from field gateway to USC
- Coordinate data availability with BST starting late May 2015

## Products & Capabilities Described

**SoilSCAPE Wireless Sensor Network**
- What it is: A wireless sensor network for automated soil moisture measurement developed by USC with prior NASA funding
- Use in this project: Ground-truth validation network for radiometer calibration and accuracy assessment
- Capabilities: Multi-depth soil moisture sensing (3 depths), wireless data transmission, network gateway at field site

**BST L-Band Radiometer on UAS**
- What it is: Microwave radiometer payload designed for airborne soil moisture remote sensing
- Use: Primary remote sensing instrument being flight-tested at the Canton, Oklahoma test site
- Ground-truth requirement: In-situ data from SoilSCAPE network needed to validate radiometer measurements

## Use Cases & Applications
- **Soil Moisture Remote Sensing Validation**: Flight testing L-band radiometer for soil moisture estimation via microwave radiometry
- **Field Campaign Location**: Canton, Oklahoma test site
- **Test Domain**: Approximately 300m × 300m field area with 10-20 measurement locations

## Key Results
This is a proposal document, not a results report. No experimental data or findings are included. The proposal was submitted for consideration by BST for funding decision.

## Executive Summary
Black Swift Technologies proposes developing a machine learning-based predictive maintenance system for USAF unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) using unsupervised learning for anomaly detection. The Phase I feasibility study will engage stakeholders at the Air Force Academy's Center for Unmanned Aircraft Systems to adapt BST's commercial monitoring system to meet specific USAF mission needs, with the goal of transitioning to a Phase II prototype that eliminates manual data tagging requirements and enables maintenance scheduling at scale.

## Technical Approach

### Core Problem & Solution
- **Problem:** UAS lack onboard monitoring and systematic maintenance. Users rely on printed owner's manual guides; critical components like servos are often unmonitored and open-loop. Telemetry data collection and analysis is time-consuming and unstandardized across platforms.
- **Solution:** Unsupervised machine learning algorithms that build models of normal aircraft behavior across varying missions and flight conditions, then flag flights that violate these models—enabling smarter predictive maintenance without requiring manual data tagging.

### Three-Layer Anomaly Detection Architecture
1. **Direct Tracking for Failures:** Real-time detection of failed sensors, low battery, lost comms, etc. (backbone of maintenance response)
2. **Supervised Learning:** Statistical methods that tie onboard telemetry to specific subsystem failures (e.g., servo motor degradation, propeller damage, icing conditions) to directly inform maintenance personnel what requires replacement
3. **Unsupervised Learning for Anomaly Detection (Primary Phase I Focus):** Flags aircraft for maintenance when performance is "out of family," applicable to whole-aircraft analysis without labeled failure datasets

### Delivery Platform
- Web-based dashboard with simplified red/yellow/green diagnostic ratings for each subsystem
- Drill-down capability for detailed information on specific systems
- Designed for accessibility by non-specialist technicians (not requiring highly skilled UAS personnel)

### Data & Implementation Strategy
- Primary approach: obtain existing USAF flight log and telemetry data for algorithm development
- Secondary capability: BST's proprietary monitoring nodes can be installed aboard candidate platforms to supplement datasets if existing USAF data proves insufficient
- Algorithm work performed on BST systems; data sourcing from USAF stakeholders

- Proprietary autopilot system developed and maintained by Dr. Elston

- Existing baseline BST system to be adapted for USAF maintenance applications

## Use Cases & Applications

- UAS maintenance scheduling and optimization
- Improving overall UAS capabilities and reliability
- Understanding and preventing UAS failures
- Supporting BVLOS (beyond visual line of sight) operations by ensuring aircraft safety above populated areas
- Addressing risk of fuel and explosive payload malfunctions

### Commercial Applications
- Routine commercial UAS operations in populated areas
- Insurance cost reduction through improved vehicle safety
- Dual-use product with both military and civilian market potential

### Specific Anomaly Detection Examples
- Compromised or failed servo motors
- Damaged propellers
- Severe weather conditions (e.g., icing buildup)
- Communication performance degradation
- "Out of family" performance across entire aircraft

## Executive Summary
USGS seeks sole-source contract with Black Swift Technologies for $80,000 to conduct multiparametric volcano monitoring operations at Nevado del Ruiz using the S2 UAS platform. BST is justified as the only U.S. vendor capable of meeting the unique combination of flight performance requirements, sensor integration, and telemetry capabilities needed for high-altitude volcanic observation during crisis situations.

## Technical Approach
The S2 UAS platform will execute volcano monitoring missions with the following technical capabilities:

**Aircraft Performance Requirements:**
- Fixed-wing, class small (<55 lbs)
- Flight ceiling: 20,000 ft
- Endurance: 90 minutes with 5 lb payload
- Operating temperature range: down to -20°C
- Corrosive environment tolerance
- Runway-independent operations
- Intermediate range: >25 km
- Low-altitude terrain following capability (150 ft AGL)
- Dynamically adaptable in-flight flight pattern creation for atmospheric sampling

**Sensor & Monitoring Payload (>2 kg capacity, 8" x 12" payload section):**
- Gas sensors: CO2, SO2, H2S
- Upward-looking UV spectrometer with real-time spectral analysis capability
- 3D wind sensor
- Temperature, relative humidity, pressure sensors
- GPS
- RTK geotagging
- Nadir photogrammetry camera
- Gimbaled or forward-looking video camera

**Telemetry & Data System:**
- High-data-rate long-distance telemetry (>10 km range)
- Real-time sensor data streaming to base station
- Base-station display software with UV spectral data analysis
- Custom payload data telemetry (not limited to integrated camera systems)

**Operational Scope:**
- Complete mission flight execution at target location
- Flight permissions and regulatory compliance
- Equipment and operator deployment logistics
- Data acquisition and cataloging
- Final reports detailing flight activities

## Products & Capabilities Described

### S2 UAS Platform
- **What it is**: Fixed-wing small UAS (<55 lbs) with advanced high-altitude capabilities
- **Proposed use**: Primary platform for multiparametric volcano monitoring at Nevado del Ruiz
- **Key specifications**: 20,000 ft ceiling, 90-min endurance, >2 kg payload capacity, runway-independent, cold-weather/corrosive-environment capable
- **Unique capability**: Interchangeable sensor nose cones allowing rapid sensor swaps without compromising data collection; integration of custom atmospheric sampling sensors and telemetry

## Use Cases & Applications

**Primary Use Case**: High-altitude volcano monitoring during volcanic crisis
- Safe observation of stratovolcano activity (Nevado del Ruiz)
- Multiparametric gas and atmospheric monitoring
- Real-time hazard assessment and forecasting
- Adaptive observation strategy based on live telemetry data

**Specific Mission Profile**:
- 10+ km flight to approach region of interest

## Executive Summary
Black Swift Technologies proposes to apply its Virtual Sensor Toolkit to develop virtual sensor redundancy for the Tempest vehicle's flight control system, identifying critical sensors for virtual redundancy, developing vehicle dynamics models, and implementing the system on BST autopilot hardware. The work includes toolkit feedback, testing support, and real-time implementation with a budget target of $40K.

## Technical Approach

**Core Task Flow:**
1. **Sensor Selection & Analysis**: Identify subset of flight control sensors where virtual redundancy provides greatest benefit based on failure susceptibility, impact on closed-loop stability/performance, and client input
2. **Failure Mode Analysis**: Characterize anticipated failure modes for selected sensors
3. **Vehicle Dynamics Modeling**: Structure existing simulation model to conform to Virtual Sensor Toolkit interface specifications; apply model simplifications for computational efficiency
4. **Noise Modeling**: Develop process and measurement noise models using toolkit-provided tools, informed by simulation and experimental data
5. **Virtual Sensor Implementation**: Generate implementation using Virtual Sensor Toolkit automation
6. **Toolkit Refinement**: Provide feedback on toolkit software and documentation based on implementation experience
7. **System Testing**: Deliver implementation and flight data to Barron Associates for testing
8. **Hardware Implementation**: Port virtual sensor implementation to Blackswift autopilot board and exercise in hardware-in-the-loop simulation
9. **Program Management**: Support technical documentation for interim and final NASA reports

## Products & Capabilities Described

**Virtual Sensor Toolkit**
- Proprietary software for automated virtual sensor implementation
- Provides interface specifications for vehicle dynamics models
- Includes tools for noise model development based on simulation/experimental data
- Automates implementation process from validated inputs

**Tempest Vehicle**
- BST UAV platform with flight control system
- Instrumented with sensors for closed-loop stability and performance
- Equipped with existing simulation model for dynamics
- Target platform for virtual redundancy implementation

**Blackswift Autopilot Board**
- Real-time capable autopilot hardware
- Target for porting and deployment of virtual sensor implementation
- Capable of hardware-in-the-loop simulation integration

## Use Cases & Applications
- Flight control system sensor redundancy and fault tolerance
- Virtual sensor implementation as backup to physical sensors
- Real-time autonomous vehicle guidance and stabilization

## Executive Summary
Dynexus Technology presents iRIS (Rapid Wideband Electrical Impedance Spectroscopy), a patented battery monitoring technology that enables State of Stability (SOS) diagnostics and prognostics for lithium-ion batteries in near real-time. BST is being approached for a potential joint development and testing agreement to integrate iRIS technology onto small drone platforms, with a phased approach beginning with a 6-month technology assessment.

## Technical Approach

**iRIS Core Technology:**
- Patented field-deployable implementation of Electrical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS)
- Active wideband AC signal excitation (0.1 Hz – 2 kHz frequency range)
- Rapid continuous monitoring capability at 10-second intervals
- Effective for online (under-load) and offline battery monitoring
- Produces 2 kB of data per scan; ~5 MB per day operation

**Measurement Capabilities:**
The technology measures:
- State of Charge (SOC)
- State of Health (SOH) with enhanced degradation tracking
- **State of Stability (SOS)** — battery health, aging, and safety characteristics (key differentiator)
- Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction
- End of Life (EOL) prediction
- Catastrophic event prediction (short-circuit, thermal runaway)

**Competitive Advantages over Existing Methods:**
- OCV (Open Circuit Voltage): Accumulates errors with capacity fade
- Coulomb Counting: Accumulates errors with capacity fade
- Single-frequency AC impedance: Requires periodic offline recalibration
- TI Impedance Track: Uses DC resistance (IR drop) but limited to SOC/capacity
- **iRIS:** Active, rapid, under-load capable; enables predictive safety assessment

**National Lab Validation:**
- Idaho National Laboratory (INL): State of Health, degradation, RUL prediction
- Sandia National Laboratory: State of Stability, battery abuse characterization, short-circuit/thermal runaway prediction

## Products & Capabilities Described

**iRIS System (Current & Roadmap)**

*Today – "Black Box" Configuration:*
- Sales price: $5k–$25k + tech support
- Target market: Stationary/UPS/Grid applications
- Full external monitoring system

*1 Year – Single Board Device:*
- Sales price: $100–$500 + software license
- Target market: e-Mobility (electric vehicles, presumably small drones)
- Reduced form factor

*2–3 Years – Integrated Circuit:*
- Sales price: TBD
- Target market: Consumer electronics
- Fully integrated chip-level implementation

**Proposed Demo Systems for Phase I:**
- iRIS-G2 system: Baseline EIS assessment and battery health signature mapping
- iRIS-G3 Ultra High-Res system: Advanced battery analytics (aging, safety/abuse, reuse signatures)

**Software/Platform Architecture:**
- iRIS-OS: Embedded software layer
- EIS via HCSD (High-Current Source Driver)
- Cloud analytics platform with AI/machine learning
- Service health management and security management modules
- Reporting and data science capabilities

## Use Cases & Applications

**Primary Proposed Application (for this JDA):**
- Small drone platform integration
- Battery safety requirements assessment for drone battery modules and packs
- Onboard vs. offboard battery monitoring exploration

**Other Potential Use Cases (mentioned):**
- Internal defect detection/characterization
- Fast charging safety and optimization
- Counterfeit battery detection
- Battery reuse assessment
- Battery cybersecurity intrusion detection

- Dr. Christophersen received R&D 100 Award (2011) for Impedance Measurement Box innovation

## Executive Summary
Black Swift Technologies proposed integrating its SwiftCore Flight Management System into a DJI S1000 and custom Raven X8 multirotor for Blue River Technology, replacing their DJI A2 flight controller with an advanced autopilot system capable of accepting external navigation input from a Phoenix Aerial AL3 RTK/fiber-optic gyro system. The project aimed to deliver two fully integrated flight-ready systems with significantly improved position tracking, waypoint navigation, and mission performance.

## Technical Approach
- **Primary integration task**: Modify SwiftCore FMS to accept external navigation inputs from Novatel SPAN OEM615 navigation board (used with Phoenix Aerial AL3 system)
- **Navigation integration**: Accept 20 Hz attitude and position updates from external nav board; implement failsafe mode to revert to onboard GPS/IMU if external nav covariance exceeds 0.05
- **Vehicle characterization**: Mass, inertia, and rotor performance measurements
- **Custom design/manufacturing**: Electrical and mechanical integration including custom mounts and wiring harnesses
- **Flight testing**: Gain tuning and performance validation/verification
- **Scope characterization**: BST classified this as "nominal vehicle-specific integration" rather than R&D, as no new customer-specific capabilities were being developed

## Products & Capabilities Described

**SwiftCore FMS:**
- Advanced autopilot system replacing DJI A2
- Accepts external navigation solutions (specifically Novatel SPAN OEM615/AL3)
- Capable of executing pre-programmed or in-flight uploaded flight plans
- Smooth banked turn execution along predetermined flight paths
- Manual control capability for recovery in high wind conditions

**SwiftCore FMS Components Included:**
- SwiftTab user interface with tablet computer
- SwiftPilot autopilot system
- SwiftStation ground station

## Flight Performance Requirements
The system was required to achieve the following under specified conditions (wind ≤10 mph, gusting to 15 mph; nav covariance <0.05):
- **Altitude tracking**: ±1 m error tolerance
- **Horizontal path deviation**: ±1 m error tolerance
- **Manual recovery capability**: Ability to conduct forward flight and landing in 20 mph winds
- **Failsafe operation**: Automatic reversion to onboard sensors if external nav degraded

## Use Cases & Applications
- Multirotor sensor-based mapping missions (primary focus)
- High-precision waypoint navigation in wind conditions
- Missions requiring improved 3D position tracking accuracy under adverse weather

## Deliverables
- 2× complete SwiftCore FMS systems with tablets and ground stations
- Full mechanical/electrical integration into both aircraft
- Custom mounts and wiring harnesses (CAD files provided)
- 4-hour training course (2 hours classroom, 2 hours field training) at BST Boulder facility
- Flight test summary report with performance metrics and validation results

## Project Schedule & Effort
- **Duration**: 8 weeks from vehicle receipt
- **Week 1**: Vehicle inspection and characterization
- **Week 2**: Mechanical/electrical design and manufacturing initiation
- **Weeks 3-4**: FMS software modification for external nav inputs
- **Week 5**: Mechanical/electrical integration and validation
- **Weeks 6-7**: Flight testing, gain tuning, performance validation, report generation
- **Week 8**: System delivery

## Executive Summary
Black Swift Technologies, in partnership with Brookhaven National Laboratory, proposes to develop an automated plume tracking and reconstruction system using AI/ML techniques applied to drone-mounted sensor imagery. The system will use neural volumetric capture methods (neural radiance fields or gaussian splatting) to reconstruct and track plume evolution from explosive test sources, with testing conducted on BST UAS platforms.

## Technical Approach

**Core Technology:**
- Neural volumetric capture, representation, and rendering techniques
- Specifically: neural radiance fields (NeRF) or gaussian splatting
- These ML/AI methods use neural networks to implicitly represent multidimensional volumes

**Key Advantages Over Traditional Methods:**
- Reconstructs volumes from sparse measurements
- Eliminates stringent geometric constraints of photogrammetry
- Reduces computational burden compared to traditional techniques
- Enables real-time analysis for navigation and multi-node (multi-drone) sampling
- Can incorporate additional measurements beyond RGB imagery
- Can be informed by governing physics

**Implementation Plan:**
- Reconstruct and track explosive test plumes from multiple non-overlapping images
- Images acquired by drone-mounted cameras
- Development and testing of software and flight planning algorithms
- Preliminary analysis through laboratory and local flight tests at BNL
- Initial operational test using sensors mounted on Black Swift UAS

**BNL's Role:**
- Software development and testing
- Flight planning implementation
- Laboratory and field testing at BNL facilities
- Reporting and documentation
- Team coordination and project execution support

## Products & Capabilities Described

**Black Swift Technologies UAS:**
- Drone platforms with mounted sensor capability
- Capable of multi-node coordinated operations
- Proposed for integration of plume tracking payload
- Operational testing platform for neural volumetric capture algorithms

## Use Cases & Applications

**Primary Application:**
- Explosive test plume tracking and reconstruction
- Source area monitoring for plume evolution analysis
- Multi-drone coordinated sampling to minimize uncertainty

**Broader Defense Applications:**
- CBRN (Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear) detection and tracking
- Threat characterization and analysis
- Autonomous plume source identification

## Notable Details

- **Sparse Data Capability:** System designed to work with non-overlapping imagery, reducing flight coordination requirements
- **Multi-drone Optimization:** Recent advances in neural volumetric techniques enable efficient multi-node sampling patterns
- **Physics-Informed:** Approach can incorporate domain knowledge about plume physics
- **Real-time Capability:** Technology supports real-time processing for autonomous navigation and adaptive flight planning
- **Phase I Scope:** Limited to preliminary analysis and initial technology demonstration; full operational testing outcomes to be determined# UAV Multispectral Vegetation Mapping for Fire Fuel Models (BOCO Proposal)

## Executive Summary
This proposal describes a research project to develop and validate UAV-based multispectral imagery for accurate mapping of wildfire fuel parameters in a Ponderosa Pine–Douglas Fir forest in Boulder County, Colorado. The project combines multispectral and RGB imagery collected by a Black Swift S1 UAV to generate 3D point clouds and vegetation classifications that can feed into wildfire behavior models (FARSITE) and emissions models (FOFEM), enabling land managers to make better fuel management and fire prediction decisions.

## Technical Approach

**Data Collection:**
- Fixed-wing UAV (Black Swift S1) equipped with 5-band multispectral sensor (MicaSense RedEdge) plus RGB camera
- Flights over two potential areas: Riverside Ranch (primary, ~640 acres) in northern Boulder County and a previously burned area in southern Boulder County
- High spatial resolution: ~3 cm/pixel for RGB; lower GSD for multispectral
- Imagery collection near local solar noon under cloudless skies to maximize signal strength
- Separate flights for RGB and multispectral data
- Field spectrometer (ASD FieldSpec) to collect reflectance measurements of ground vegetation for calibration

**Data Processing:**
- Mosaicking with Pix4D software (includes radiometric and atmospheric correction to convert radiance to reflectance)
- Image analysis with ENVI software including:
  - Vegetation index calculations
  - Principal component analysis
  - Supervised classification
  - Feature extraction
- Production of 3D point clouds from photogrammetric processing of multi-perspective imagery
- Vegetation species mapping output (grass, shrubs, trees)

**Validation:**
- Field spectrometer measurements to calibrate imagery
- Field visits to evaluate classification accuracy

## Products & Capabilities Described

### Black Swift S1 UAV
- Fixed-wing platform
- 1-hour flight time
- Considerably quieter than multi-copters
- Capable of covering 640 acres at ~3 cm/pixel with RGB camera in single flight
- Can carry multiple sensor payloads (multispectral and RGB)

### SwiftCore Flight Management System
- Ground station for UAV flight control

### MicaSense RedEdge Multispectral Sensor
- 5-band sensor
- Includes vegetation red edge capability
- Used to map vegetation types and discriminate fuel groups

## Use Cases & Applications

**Primary Application: Wildfire Fuel Mapping**
- Map primary fuel groups: grass, shrubs, trees
- Determine secondary fuel parameters from 3D point clouds:
  - Tree density, size, canopy closure, height, species
  - Canopy height, canopy bulk density, available canopy fuel
- Generate spatially explicit fuel layers for input into:
  - FARSITE (wildfire behavior model)
  - FOFEM (fire emissions model)

**End User Benefits:**
- Enable land managers to make smart fuel management decisions
- Improve fire behavior prediction capabilities
- More accurate crown fire risk assessment
- More accurate smoke emission predictions

## Key Results
No results reported; this is a proposal for work to be conducted. Project schedule specified:
- UAV data collection: Spring 2018
- Field accuracy checks: Late summer 2018
- Final report delivery: Before December 9, 2018

## Project Location & Scope

**Primary Study Area: Riverside Ranch**
- Located in northern Boulder County, approximately 5 miles west of Lyons and 1.5 miles north of Highway 7
- Approximately 640 acres
- Elevation: 6,600'–8,000'
- Vegetation: Ponderosa Pine–Douglas Fir forest
- Remote location with minimal visitation expected

**Secondary Area (if funds/time allow):**
- Previously burned area in southern Boulder County (location pending)

**Timing Rationale:**
- Spring collection: Maximizes phenological differences between species, improving species differentiation accuracy
- Late summer collection (if feasible): Captures additional phenological differences

## Notable Details

**Hypotheses & Innovation Claims:**
- High spatial resolution UAV multispectral imagery should provide more precise species and fuel maps than satellite data
- UAV-derived point clouds from photogrammetry can compete with lidar-derived point clouds for 3D vegetation metrics
- Finer spatial resolution should enable accurate quantification of vegetation metrics critical to fuel models

**Budget Summary:**
- Total project cost: $8,600
- Equipment already procured (S1 UAV, SwiftCore, ASD FieldSpec)
- New software subscriptions: Pix4D ($700/month), ENVI
- Labor: Field work ($3,000), mosaicking ($400), image analysis ($4,800), report writing ($400)

**Regulatory/Permitting Requirements:**
- UAS Authorization Application required for flying over Boulder County Open Space
- Research Permit required for work on county open space

**Collaboration:**
- Partnership between Black Swift Technologies (UAV platform and operations) and HSI Geo/Joe Zamudio (remote sensing expertise and analysis)

## Executive Summary
Black Swift Technologies proposes to advance autonomous UAS operations in harsh environments by automating wind-aware flight planning, improving the manufacturability of the S2-VTOL vertical takeoff and landing system, and enhancing the SwiftTab user interface for flexible payload data management. The work builds on Phase II-E results demonstrating the only successful visual observations of a target volcano during challenging conditions, with goals of enabling routine, worldwide scientific missions in difficult weather and terrain.

## Technical Approach

**Key Innovation:** Automating mission management in harsh conditions to reduce dependency on highly trained operators and months of preparation.

**Four Primary Objectives:**

1. **Intelligent Wind-Aware Flight Planning:** Implement real-time environmental assessment combined with predictive modeling to adjust flight paths dynamically, minimizing energy usage during convective storms and mountainous terrain operations. Integration into SwiftCore firmware with flight demonstrations.

2. **User Interface Enhancements:** Update SwiftTab app to support flexible payload integration, displaying telemetry from interchangeable payloads and enabling payload control through a common operating picture.

3. **Advanced Mission Planning:** Automate terrain and communication limitation analysis in flight planning and flight control systems, similar to wind-aware planning approach.

4. **S2-VTOL Manufacturability Improvements:** Simplify construction and reduce cost of the S2-VTOL prototype while retaining its primary advantage: ability to launch and land in strong wind events nearly anywhere.

## Products & Capabilities Described

**S2-VTOL:**
- Vertical takeoff and landing small UAS capable of operations in strong wind conditions
- Can launch and land nearly anywhere
- Prototype demonstrated during Phase II-E volcano monitoring mission
- Proposed improvements: simplified construction, reduced manufacturing cost

**SwiftCore Firmware:**
- Flight control and navigation software
- Targeted for wind-aware flight planning implementation
- Real-time environmental assessment and predictive modeling capabilities

**SwiftTab App:**
- Mission planning and telemetry display interface
- Supports interchangeable payloads
- Planned enhancements for flexible payload data management and control

## Use Cases & Applications

**Primary Mission (Phase II-E Background):**
- Volcano monitoring with visual observations
- Achieved only successful visual observations of target volcano during calendar year despite difficult conditions
- Required months of flight planning preparation
- Frequent real-time wind observations necessary during flights to maintain safe battery margins for return and landing

**NASA Applications:**
- Tropospheric Chemistry Program (TCP)
- Applied Sciences Air Quality Program
- CALIPSO (Cloud-Aerosol Lidar and Infrared Pathfinder Satellite Observations) mission support
- Aura mission
- CATS (Cloud-Aerosol Transport System)
- OCO-2/3 (Orbital Carbon Observatory) programs
- Earth Ventures airborne field campaigns
- Volcanic and wildfire observations (JPL and NASA Ames partnerships)

**Non-NASA Applications:**
- USGS, NOAA, DOE, National Weather Service
- Wildfire monitoring and support (particulate sampling, severe turbulence environments)
- Commercial multi-hole probe sensor market

## Key Results (Phase II-E Context)
- Demonstrated first and only successful visual observations of target volcano during challenging conditions
- Validated small UAS utility for routine scientific data gathering
- Identified critical need for automation: current operations require exceptionally knowledgeable, well-trained teams and months of preparation
- Demonstrated necessity of real-time wind monitoring and custom software to ensure safe battery margins

## Notable Details

- **Competitive Advantage:** S2-VTOL's strong wind launch/landing capability addresses a significant limiting factor for small UAS operations
- **Automation Focus:** Primary innovation emphasizes reducing operational complexity and team expertise requirements to enable "routine and worldwide" deployment
- **Interchangeable Payloads:** System designed for flexibility across multiple scientific instruments and missions

## Executive Summary
Building on Phase II-E work conducting volcano monitoring with small UAS, this Phase III effort proposes to automate mission capabilities for harsh environment operations. The focus is implementing intelligent flight planning for strong winds, improving the user interface for payload management, automating terrain/communication-aware mission planning, and improving manufacturability of the S2-VTOL platform to enable routine worldwide deployment in difficult weather conditions.

## Technical Approach
Four main technical objectives:

1. **Wind-Aware Intelligent Flight Planning**: Implement real-time environmental assessment and predictive modeling to inform dynamic flight path adjustments that minimize energy usage. Changes will be integrated into SwiftCore firmware and demonstrated in flight testing. This addresses the current manual requirement for constant wind monitoring and battery margin calculations.

2. **User Interface Improvements**: Enhance SwiftTab app to provide flexible telemetry display and payload control. A common operating picture is needed to accommodate interchangeable payloads and support scientific data management for various mission types.

3. **Automated Terrain & Communications Planning**: Extend mission planning and flight control automation to account for terrain navigation and communication constraints, similar to wind-aware planning. Addresses limitations of manual, months-long mission preparation currently required.

4. **S2-VTOL Manufacturability Improvements**: Refine the S2-VTOL design to simplify construction and reduce cost while maintaining the key capability of launching/landing in strong wind conditions—currently identified as a limiting factor for small UAS operations.

## Products & Capabilities Described

**S2-VTOL**
- Prototype vertical takeoff/landing small UAS platform
- Key advantage: ability to launch and land nearly anywhere during strong wind events
- Proposed improvements: simplified manufacturing, reduced price
- Addresses a current limiting factor for small UAS operations in harsh conditions

**SwiftCore (Firmware)**
- Flight control and mission execution firmware
- Proposed enhancements: wind-aware flight planning, real-time environmental assessment, predictive modeling, automated mission adjustments

**SwiftTab (App)**
- Ground station/user interface application
- Current limitation: not flexible enough for multi-payload operations
- Proposed improvements: common operating picture, flexible telemetry display, payload control interface

## Use Cases & Applications

**Primary:**
- Volcano monitoring (specifically referenced as Phase II-E application)
- Operations in convective storms
- Mountainous terrain flight

**Implied broader applications:**
- Routine scientific data gathering in harsh/difficult weather conditions
- Worldwide deployment missions
- Missions with challenging terrain navigation and communication constraints

## Notable Details

- **Phase II-E Context**: Previous phase achieved "only visual observations of the target volcano during that calendar year," demonstrating mission success but revealing operational complexity
- **Current Operational Burden**: Mission planning currently requires months of preparation; flight execution requires a "very knowledgeable and well trained team" with frequent real-time wind monitoring and custom software calculations
- **Automation Goal**: Intent is to make routine, worldwide harsh-environment operations viable by automating capabilities currently requiring expert manual management
- **VTOL Advantage**: Strong wind launch/landing capability identified as competitive advantage and current operational limiting factor for small UAS
- **Interchangeable Payloads**: System architecture supports multiple scientific payload configurations

## Executive Summary
Black Swift Technologies proposes development of a VTOL (vertical takeoff and land) variant of the S2 XT UAS specifically designed for sampling volcanic ash clouds and measuring atmospheric properties in harsh environments. Building on Phase II work that demonstrated the fixed-wing S2 XT platform, Phase II-E will add vertical takeoff/landing capability in winds up to 30 mph and conduct a demonstration flight campaign at Makushin Volcano in Alaska.

## Technical Approach

### VTOL Enhancement of S2 XT
The core technical approach involves three primary work elements:

1. **Airframe Design**: Modification of the existing S2 XT fixed-wing airframe to integrate 4 rotors for VTOL capability while maintaining the fixed-wing performance characteristics that enable harsh environment operations.

2. **High-Wind VTOL Algorithms**: Development of hybrid landing algorithms that combine rotor control with fixed-wing aerodynamic surfaces to enable landing in winds up to 30 mph. This hybrid approach preserves the S2 XT's inherent capability to operate in severe environmental conditions.

3. **Demonstration Flight Campaign**: Flight operations at Makushin Volcano in Alaska to validate VTOL S2 XT performance and collect scientific data, including deployment of new real-time data visualization capability.

### Scientific Measurement Capabilities
The integrated system will measure:
- Trace gases
- Particulate sizing and density
- Pressure, temperature, humidity
- 3D winds
- EO (electro-optical) and thermal imagery and video

## Products & Capabilities Described

### S2 XT (VTOL Variant)
- **What it is**: A hybrid VTOL/fixed-wing UAS derived from the commercial S2 airframe
- **Proposed use**: Sampling of volcanic plumes; atmospheric monitoring in harsh environments
- **Key specifications**: 
  - VTOL capability in winds up to 30 mph
  - Transition to forward flight for extended range operations
  - Integrated sensor suite for multi-parameter atmospheric measurement
  - Designed for nomadic field campaigns

### SwiftCore Flight Management System
- **What it is**: The avionics/flight control core of the platform
- **Status**: Proven in field operations; commercial baseline
- **Characteristics**: Cost-effective, powerful, easy-to-operate

### Sensor Suite
- Multi-parameter atmospheric measurement package (gases, particulates, meteorological parameters)
- EO and thermal imaging capability
- Real-time data visualization system (noted as "new" capability)
- Multi-hole probe sensor (noted as having commercial market potential)

## Use Cases & Applications

### Primary: Volcanic Monitoring
- Sampling of volcanic ash clouds and plumes
- Demonstration planned at Makushin Volcano, Alaska
- Trace gas measurement in volcanic emissions
- Particulate characterization from volcanic activity

### Secondary Applications

**Government Agencies**:
- USGS: Volcanic and geological monitoring
- NOAA: Atmospheric research
- DOE: Energy/environmental programs
- National Weather Service: Weather observation

**Operational Use Cases**:
- Wildfire monitoring and support (particulate measurement, operation in severe turbulence)
- Hazardous environment operations (where manned aircraft cannot safely operate)

**Scientific Programs**:
- Tropospheric Chemistry Program (TCP)
- Applied Sciences Air Quality Program
- CALIPSO, Aura, CATS, OCO-2/3 missions (supporting airborne field campaigns)
- Earth Ventures program

## Technical Rationale

The document emphasizes that the VTOL capability enhancement does **not sacrifice** the S2 XT's proven ability to operate in harsh environments through the hybrid algorithm approach. This is positioned as a key innovation—maintaining forward-flight performance characteristics (which enable extended range and rough-air penetration) while adding VTOL flexibility for deployment in remote locations without prepared landing sites.

## Executive Summary
Black Swift Technologies proposes to design and build a gondola-launched fixed-wing glider capable of operating in Venus's lower atmosphere beneath the cloud layers. The glider would complement balloon-based atmospheric measurements by providing high-speed (50-70 m/s) station-keeping capability and surface reconnaissance via near-infrared imaging, overcoming the mobility limitations of balloon platforms while remaining small and light enough to serve as a low-risk mission component.

## Technical Approach

**Core Concept:**
- Small, fixed-wing glider deployed from a high-altitude balloon gondola
- Designed for sustained operations in Venus lower atmosphere (beneath cloud layers)
- High-speed cruise (50-70 m/s) enables station keeping with upper atmosphere balloon
- Can carry scientific payload for in situ measurements and remote sensing

**Key Technical Tasks:**
1. Vehicle aerodynamic design optimized for Venus atmospheric conditions
2. Aircraft construction materials identification for high-temperature environment
3. Sensor and avionics selection for harsh Venus conditions
4. Relative navigation system design for station keeping with balloon
5. Candidate system simulation to demonstrate concept-of-operation
6. Commercial potential and product viability assessment

**Navigation & Control:**
- Development of sensors and control algorithms to maintain station-keeping position relative to the balloon
- Relative navigation system to enable coordinated operations with balloon platform

## Products & Capabilities Described

**Venus Lower Atmosphere Glider:**
- **What it is:** Small fixed-wing aircraft designed for deployment from balloon gondola
- **Proposed use:** Complement balloon measurements; image Venus surface through near-infrared wavelengths; conduct in situ experiments in lower atmosphere
- **Key specifications:**
  - Cruise speed: 50-70 m/s
  - Small enough to fit in aeroshell voids (enabling carriage on missions without dedicated balloon payload)
  - Weight and size constrained by payload integration requirements
  - Must operate in high-temperature environment with minimal power budget
- **Sensors:** Remote observing sensors (details to be selected) for surface imaging at near-infrared wavelengths; in situ atmospheric sensors (TBD)

## Use Cases & Applications

**NASA Applications:**
- Venus atmospheric science missions with balloon platforms
- Technology demonstrator providing low-risk, high-reward science component
- Carriage in aeroshell voids on Venus missions (even those without dedicated balloon payload)
- Aerial reconnaissance of Venus surface beneath clouds

**Non-NASA Applications:**
- NOAA hurricane observation and monitoring (balloon-borne platform with station-keeping glider)
- Severe convective storm research and monitoring
- Severe weather research platforms requiring persistent atmospheric presence

## Key Milestones
1. Complete initial material selection for aircraft construction
2. Complete aircraft aerodynamic design and scientific payload selection
3. Complete sensor selection and develop control algorithm for station keeping
4. Demonstrate desired concept-of-operation in simulation

## Notable Details

- **Innovation driver:** Venus surface imaging in near-infrared has never been achieved due to thick cloud layers; gliders overcome balloon mobility limitations while remaining small enough to integrate into existing mission architecture
- **Risk mitigation:** Small, light vehicle design allows deployment as secondary payload with minimal mission penalty
- **Dual-use potential:** Platform designed for Venus but explicitly noted for NOAA and severe weather applications on Earth

## Executive Summary
Black Swift Technologies proposes developing an advanced sensor fusion system for real-time 3D hazard mapping that enables fixed-wing UAS to safely operate at low altitudes in terrain-challenged environments. The system uses pseudo-lidar technology based on stereo depth neural networks to provide terrain and obstacle awareness, addressing a significant gap in autonomous fixed-wing operations over rugged terrain where multi-rotor aircraft are currently the only viable option.

## Technical Approach
- **Core Technology**: Pseudo-lidar capability using deep neural networks trained on stereo imagery
- **Sensor Fusion Strategy**: Combines stereo camera imagery with DEM (Digital Elevation Model) data for enhanced terrain classification
- **Implementation Path**: 
  - Generate training datasets for neural network development
  - Train and evaluate two stereo depth DNN versions (stereo-only and stereo+DEM fusion)
  - Select lightweight, low-cost sensors and compute hardware suitable for small UAS
  - Integrate and test on flight hardware, demonstrating real-time performance at fixed-wing flight speeds
  - Design mechanical integration and prepare flight certification materials for Phase II testing on BST aircraft

## Products & Capabilities Described

**S2 UAS**
- BST's fixed-wing platform already tested in multiple NASA campaigns
- Identified need for terrain-contouring system during volcanic plume sampling mission in Costa Rica
- Proposed as initial platform for incorporating the new terrain-following technology

**Pseudo-Lidar Terrain/Object Classification System**
- Generates low-altitude 3D hazard maps in real-time
- Lightweight and low-cost design for integration on small UAS
- Real-time performance requirement at fixed-wing aircraft speeds
- Provides terrain and obstacle awareness for autonomous low-altitude flight

## Use Cases & Applications

**NASA Applications**
- Volcanic plume measurements with terrain contouring
- High-resolution soil moisture measurements
- Surface flux calculations above arctic tundra
- Legacy NASA UAS integration

**Non-NASA Applications**
- Infrastructure inspection with reliable low-altitude flight capability
- Leak detection systems
- Mountain mapping in rugged terrain
- Rock slide mitigation planning
- Avalanche prediction support

## Technical Objectives & Deliverables

**Phase I Objectives:**
1. Identify and validate algorithms and training data for real-time pseudo-lidar operation at fixed-wing flight speeds
2. Develop preliminary design of pseudo-lidar and terrain/object classification system
3. Integrate, test, and evaluate pseudo-lidar capability
4. Design mechanical system and prepare flight certification materials for Phase II

**Milestones:**
- Completion of training data library
- Build and evaluation of stereo DNN (two versions: stereo-only and stereo+DEM fusion)
- Sensor and compute hardware evaluation and selection
- Real-time system demonstration on flight hardware

## Notable Details
- Problem Statement: Fixed-wing UAS have been restricted to operational areas without obstacles or significant terrain variation; manual multi-rotor operation remains the primary solution for challenging terrain
- Market Positioning: System positioned as transferable to legacy NASA platforms and commercial applications (infrastructure inspection, GIS/surveying)

## Executive Summary
Black Swift Technologies proposes to develop CASED, a system to measure winds and turbulence in the lower 5,000 feet of atmosphere by adapting existing Eddy Dissipation Rate (EDR) algorithms to small fixed-wing UAS. The system leverages BST's historical flight data and partners with NCAR to fill critical data gaps needed for safe integration of Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) and UAS into national airspace through UAS Traffic Management (UTM) systems.

## Technical Approach
- Adapt existing EDR (Eddy Dissipation Rate) algorithms to work on small fixed-wing UAS platforms
- Utilize BST's extensive historical flight dataset to validate algorithm performance on UAS-scale data
- Identify and document hardware, sensor, and processing requirements for accurate EDR measurements
- Implement EDR algorithm on BST's S2 fixed-wing UAS
- Perform bench-top demonstration and validation before Phase II flight testing
- Develop Interface Control Document (ICD) for system integration

## Products & Capabilities Described

### S2 UAS
- BST's fixed-wing UAS platform
- Proposed as testbed for CASED system
- Historical flight data available for algorithm development and validation
- Proposed to carry CASED hardware/sensors for Phase II flight testing

### CASED System
- Module to be added to any UAS to measure and report winds and turbulence
- Includes EDR algorithm implementation, sensors, processing hardware, and communications interfaces
- Designed to operate with minimal computational requirements
- Output: near real-time wind and turbulence data for distribution to AAM/UAS operators

## Use Cases & Applications

### NASA Applications
- Fill critical data void in wind and turbulence observations in lowest 5,000 feet of atmosphere
- Support UAS Traffic Management (UTM) system accuracy by providing 3D wind/turbulence profiles

## Document Metadata
- Type: SBIR Phase I Briefing Chart
- Client/Agency: NASA
- Program/Solicitation: NASA SBIR 2021, Topic A2.03-1878
- Date: January 2021 (submitted)
- BST Products/Systems Referenced: SwiftFlow probe, AeroPod, ABLGrid tethersonde system
- Key Personnel: Maciej Stachura (PI), Jack Elston (contact)

## Executive Summary
Black Swift Technologies proposes ABLGrid, a networked tethersonde system for distributed atmospheric measurements within the atmospheric boundary layer (ABL). The system addresses the critical need for hyper-local, in-situ weather observations to support both recreational and commercial UAS operations, as well as broader weather forecasting and nowcasting applications.

## Technical Approach
The ABLGrid tethersonde is based on NASA-licensed AeroPod design, modified from BST's SwiftFlow probe. Key technical elements include:
- **Sensor Suite**: Temperature, relative humidity (RH), pressure, and 3D wind measurements
- **Active Control Design**: Completed during Phase I for stability and functionality
- **Radio/Wireless Network**: Custom radio link design enabling data dissemination between networked tethersondes and central location
- **Deployment Method**: Tether-suspended from balloon for atmospheric profiling
- **Data System**: Networked architecture supporting real-time data aggregation for nowcasts and forecasts

## Products & Capabilities Described

### ABLGrid Tethersonde System
- **What it is**: A networked atmospheric measurement platform combining a tethersonde probe with balloon-tether deployment and wireless data network
- **Proposed Use**: Distributed deployment for hyper-local atmospheric monitoring; addresses gap left by UAS weather limitations and lack of fine-scale forecasting
- **Key Specifications**: Full ABL sensor suite (temp, RH, pressure, 3D wind); active control; wireless network topology; ease of deployment with fewer operational restrictions than UAS
- **TRL Level**: Estimated advancement through Phase I development

### SwiftFlow Probe (as basis)
- Serves as foundation design for tethersonde adaptation
- Provides measurement capabilities

## Use Cases & Applications

### NASA Applications
- Planetary boundary layer (PBL) measurements, identified as key target in 2017 National Academies Earth Science Decadal Survey
- Enables low-cost, easily deployable alternative to UAS with fewer operational restrictions

### Non-NASA Applications
- **Weather Forecasting**: Local airports, citizen scientists, educational groups
- **Government**: Local, state, and federal entities requiring weather data
- **Industries**: Precision agriculture, transportation (applications relying on hyper-local weather products)

## Key Technical Objectives & Deliverables

**Objectives:**
1. Tethersonde design leveraging NASA-licensed AeroPod and BST SwiftFlow
2. Active control design development and demonstration
3. Data dissemination system between network nodes and central location
4. Prototype testing on tether-balloon system

**Tasks:**
1. ABLGrid tethersonde preliminary design
2. Active control design, implementation, testing
3. Radio link design and implementation
4. Integration, testing/demonstration, evaluation
5. Commercial potential and product viability exploration
6. Report preparation and submission

**Milestones:**
1. SwiftFlow/AeroPod-derived tethersonde design completion
2. Active control design and bench-top testing completion
3. Radio/wireless network topology demonstration
4. ABLGrid tethersonde demonstration in relevant environment

## Notable Details
- **Problem Addressed**: Wind and turbulence evaluation gap for UAS operations; lack of hyper-local meteorological forecasting systems
- **Competitive Advantage**: Networked approach enabling distributed data collection; lower operational restrictions than UAS; cost-effective for widespread deployment
- **NASA Connection**: Uses NASA-licensed AeroPod design, targets priorities from National Academies decadal survey
- **Multi-stakeholder Appeal**: Addresses needs across recreational/commercial operators, government, academia, and private industry
- **Contact**: Jack Elston, elstonj@bst.aero, (720) 638-9656# A Scalable System for Supplemental Meteorological Information Using UAS-based Wind and Eddy Dissipation Measurement

## Document Metadata
- Type: SBIR Phase I Proposal Briefing Chart
- Client/Agency: NASA
- Program/Solicitation: 2022 SBIR, Topic A2.03-2738
- Date: March 9, 2022
- BST Products/Systems Referenced: S2 (fixed-wing UAS)
- Key Personnel: Jack Elston (PI, Black Swift Technologies)

## Executive Summary
Black Swift Technologies proposes developing WATCHES (Winds Aloft, Turbulence Characteristics and Hazardous Eddy Surveillance), a scalable module to measure winds and turbulence in the lowest 5,000 feet of atmosphere using small UAS. In partnership with NCAR, the system will adapt eddy dissipation rate (EDR) algorithms to fixed-wing UAS platforms to fill critical data gaps needed for safe Urban Air Mobility (AAM/UAM) and UAS Traffic Management (UTM) operations.

## Technical Approach
- **Algorithm Adaptation**: Leverage BST's historical flight data collection to adapt EDR (Eddy Dissipation Rate) algorithms from manned aircraft to small fixed-wing UAS; assess whether existing UAS flight data meets EDR algorithm requirements
- **System Requirements Definition**: Identify and document computational power, sensors, and communications interfaces necessary for accurate EDR measurements
- **Hardware Development & Testing**: Develop bench-top demonstration running on flight-ready hardware; assemble and test complete WATCHES setup on S2 platform for Phase II flight testing
- **Vertical Winds Integration**: Install vertical winds algorithm on Black Swift fixed-wing UAS
- **Validation & Commercial Viability**: Perform validation testing; explore commercial potential and product viability

## Products & Capabilities Described

### S2 (Black Swift Fixed-Wing UAS)
- Proposed platform for WATCHES integration and flight testing
- Will carry the WATCHES measurement module with EDR and vertical winds algorithms
- Historical flight data from S2 will be used to validate and refine algorithms

### WATCHES System
- Modular design intended to be added to any small UAS
- Measures winds and turbulence profiles in lower atmosphere
- Provides real-time data dissemination to AAM/UAS/UAM operators
- Core capability: eddy dissipation rate measurement for turbulence characterization

## Use Cases & Applications

### NASA/Government Applications
- **UAS Traffic Management (UTM)**: Enable accurate 3D wind and turbulence profiles for safe UAS integration into national airspace
- **Urban Air Mobility (AAM/UAM) Safety**: Provide real-time turbulence hazard data to operators
- **Meteorological Research**: Fill data void in lower atmosphere observations (0-5,000 ft); support advances in short-term Numerical Weather Prediction
- **Scalable Monitoring**: Scale measurement capability as AAM industry grows to enable increased atmospheric sampling at minimal cost

### Commercial Applications
- **Direct Operator Subscription**: Real-time turbulence data to AAM/UAS/UAM operators
- **Third-Party Services**: Distribution through commercial weather/data services
- **Scientific Data Mining**: Commercial scientific applications

## Phase I Objectives & Deliverables

**Objective 1**: Adapt EDR algorithm for small fixed-wing UAS using BST historical flight data

**Objective 2**: Identify and document system requirements (processing power, sensors, communications)

**Objective 3**: Bench-top demonstration of WATCHES on Phase II flight-ready hardware

**Key Tasks**:
1. Implement wind and turbulence algorithms
2. Develop Interface Control Document
3. Develop plan to extend WATCHES capability
4. Install vertical winds algorithm on BST fixed-wing UAS
5. Validation testing
6. Explore commercial potential and product viability
7. Prepare and submit reports

**Phase I Milestones**:
1. Demonstrate WATCHES using S2 historical data
2. Complete Interface Control Document
3. Finalize hardware and sensor requirements for fixed-wing UAS
4. Assemble and test flight-ready WATCHES setup for S2 (Phase II entry)

## Notable Details
- **Partnership**: NCAR collaboration for algorithm development
- **Data Gap Focus**: Addresses documented shortage of wind/turbulence observations in lowest 5,000 feet of atmosphere
- **Timing**: Aligned with surge in commercial AAM/UAS expansion and national airspace integration requirements
- **Scalability**: Design emphasizes minimal cost for data collection as industry grows
- **Technology Transfer Pathway**: Clear path from Phase I algorithm validation through Phase II flight testing to commercial deployment# All Weather UAS for Long Term Unattended Environmental Observations

## Document Metadata
- **Type:** SBIR Phase I Proposal Briefing Chart
- **Client/Agency:** NASA
- **Program/Solicitation:** NASA SBIR 2022, Topic S16.04-2763 (Extreme Environments)
- **Date:** March 9, 2022
- **BST Products/Systems Referenced:** S2, S2-VTOL, S3
- **Key Personnel:** Jack Elston (PI)

## Executive Summary
Black Swift Technologies proposes the S3 UAS, a next-generation uncrewed aircraft evolved from the S2-VTOL platform, designed for all-weather operations and long-duration unattended environmental monitoring missions lasting days to months. The innovation centers on severe weather capability (high-speed performance, icing/precipitation resistance) and autonomous persistent operations (onboard solar charging enabling multi-day missions without return to base).

## Technical Approach

### Extreme Weather Redesign
- Complete redesign of S2-VTOL airframe for severe weather operations
- New aerodynamic design optimized for high dash speeds to overcome strong winds
- Improved climb performance for strong downdrafts
- Structural design and control geometry for safe operation in strong turbulence
- Heavy precipitation and icing-resistant modifications

### Systems Modifications
- **Pitot/Static System:** New design rated for heavy precipitation and icing environments
- **Waterproofing:** Extended waterproofing of aircraft with minimal mass increase
- **Onboard Intelligence Monitoring:** Multiple cameras for:
  - Environmental and terrain monitoring
  - Wing icing detection
  - Propulsion system icing monitoring

### Long-Duration Capability
- Autonomous landing system
- Onboard battery recharge via integrated solar panels in wings
- Persistent operations model: aircraft remains deployed and cycles through multiple flights over extended periods rather than returning to base after each sortie

### Phase I Work Plan
- Complete new wing and tail aerodynamic design/analysis
- Structural CAD modeling of redesigned components
- System design modifications for precipitation/icing environments
- Hardware/sensor selection for onboard intelligence monitoring system
- Requirements evaluation for icing detection systems

## Products & Capabilities Described

### S3 UAS
- **Description:** Next-generation small uncrewed aircraft evolved from S2-VTOL platform
- **Key Innovation:** Combination of extreme weather resilience and autonomous persistent operations
- **Proposed Capabilities:**
  - All-weather operation (severe turbulence, heavy precipitation, icing)
  - High dash speeds for wind penetration
  - Strong downdraft climb performance
  - Autonomous recharge via solar power
  - Multi-day to multi-month mission endurance without operator presence
  - Onboard environmental monitoring and health monitoring cameras

### Referenced Legacy Systems
- **S2:** Earlier generation UAS with proven deployment record
- **S2-VTOL:** Vertical takeoff/landing variant; basis for S3 redesign; currently used for volcano monitoring and satellite calibration

## Use Cases & Applications

### NASA Applications
1. **Volcano Monitoring:** Expansion of existing S2/S2-VTOL missions with enhanced all-weather capability and multi-week deployment potential
2. **Satellite Calibration:** MALIBU project; S3 enables larger area coverage and demonstration of weeks-to-months persistent mission concepts

### Non-NASA Applications
1. **Pipeline Methane Leak Detection:** 
   - Inspection of hundreds of miles of pipeline per day
   - Autonomous operation eliminates per-flight human operator costs
   - Significant greenhouse gas monitoring capability
   - Partnership established with sensor company for delivery

## Notable Details

- **Competitive Advantage:** S3 represents a "revolutionary change in capabilities of small UAS for Earth observing" by combining extreme weather resilience with persistent autonomous operations—a capability gap in current small UAS market
- **Leveraging Heritage:** Proposal builds on BST's proven S2/S2-VTOL deployment record across difficult missions
- **Funding TRL Statement:** "TRL Estimated" header present but TRL value not populated in this briefing chart
- **Commercial Partnership:** BST already partnered with sensor company for methane detection payload integration
- **Operational Model Shift:** The persistent operations concept (autonomous recharge, multi-day deployment, no return-to-base requirement) represents a fundamental change in how Earth observation UAS missions are conducted

## Technical Risks/Challenges Implicit in Proposal
- Icing protection and detection in heavy precipitation environments
- Structural integrity for sustained turbulence operations
- Solar panel integration weight/performance balance
- Autonomous landing reliability in extreme conditions
- Multi-week power management and system reliability# A Common Operating Picture and Flight Demonstrations for UAS Integration With Active Wildfire Operations

## Document Metadata
- Type: SBIR Phase I Proposal / Briefing Chart
- Client/Agency: NASA
- Program/Solicitation: NASA SBIR 2022, Topic A3.04-2771
- Date: March 9, 2022
- BST Products/Systems Referenced: Small UAS platforms (unspecified model), UAS for wildfire characterization
- Key Personnel: Maciej Stachura (PI), Jack Elston (BST contact)

## Executive Summary
Black Swift Technologies proposes to develop a common operating picture (COP) and airspace management solution for unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) operating in active wildfire response environments. The solution will integrate existing software (ATAK) with NASA's UTM research and BST's experience in UAS operations to enable safe, coordinated flight of multiple manned and unmanned assets while providing enhanced situational awareness for fire characterization and management.

## Technical Approach
BST's approach leverages:
- **Existing software platforms** already deployed in wildland firefighting (specifically ATAK—Army Tactical Operations Center)
- **NASA UTM research** conducted for urban airspace integration
- **BST's prior experience** in atmospheric sampling, UAS operations in extreme environments, and wildfire model improvement
- Development of a **simulation and flight test-bed** to validate the integrated system
- Creation of standardized **interface definitions** to enable data dissemination beyond typical near real-time EO/IR imagery
- User interface design informed by BST's previous UAS development experience

**Key focus areas:**
- Airspace management and deconfliction between manned and unmanned assets
- Real-time data dissemination for situational awareness
- Safe standoff maintenance between airborne assets
- Integration of diverse sensor data for fire state assessment

## Products & Capabilities Described
- **BST Small UAS**: Described as "highly capable" platforms designed for wildfire response; capable of operations in hazardous environments with particulates and severe turbulence
- **UAS-based sensing systems**: Referenced but not detailed in this briefing chart; intended to provide data beyond standard EO/IR imagery
- **Software integration capability**: BST's experience developing user interfaces for UAS systems

## Use Cases & Applications

### Primary Application
- **Active wildfire monitoring and response**: Multi-asset coordination, real-time airspace management, fire characterization and model refinement during active fire suppression operations

### Secondary Applications (Non-NASA)
- **Volcano monitoring**: Leveraging capability to operate in hazardous environments with particulates and turbulence
- **Cooperative UTM applications**: Federal and commercial airspace integration efforts (unspecified)

### NASA Cross-Cutting Applications
- Potential users beyond NASA Ames include:
  - Tropospheric Chemistry Program (TCP)
  - Applied Sciences Air Quality Program
  - CALIPSO mission
  - Aura mission
  - CATS (Cloud-Aerosol Transport System)
  - OCO-3 (Orbiting Carbon Observatory)
  - Earth Ventures program for airborne field campaigns

## Phase I Milestones & Deliverables

1. **Summary document**: Currently used software for wildfire UTM and data dissemination
2. **Summary document**: Desired UAS-based sensing systems
3. **Interface Definition Document**: Specifications for system integration
4. **Flight authorization documentation**: Necessary approvals for Phase II flight demonstrations
5. **Functioning simulation**: Fully operational simulation environment with BST UAS models

## Notable Details
- **Software compatibility**: Proposal emphasizes building on existing widely-deployed tools (ATAK) rather than developing from scratch, ensuring field readiness and user familiarity
- **Informed by agency research**: Direct reference to leveraging NASA's UTM work to avoid duplication and ensure integration with broader national airspace initiatives
- **Multi-stakeholder approach**: Proposes working with "several of the leading current operators" in wildland firefighting to ensure operational relevance
- **Hazardous environment capability**: BST differentiates itself on ability to operate reliably in particulate-rich, high-turbulence environments typical of active fire zones
- **Expansion beyond imagery**: Proposal seeks to move beyond traditional EO/IR data to provide richer situational picture for fire state assessment

## Innovation Claim
The innovation is framed as addressing a specific gap: UAS cannot currently participate fully in wildfire operations due to lack of standardized data dissemination and airspace management solutions tailored to the wildfire domain, despite extensive UTM development for urban airspace.# Uncrewed Aircraft System Data Assimilation for Improved Wildland Fire Fighting Decision Support

## Document Metadata
- Type: NASA SBIR Phase I Proposal Briefing Chart
- Client/Agency: NASA
- Program/Solicitation: NASA SBIR 2023, Topic A3.02-1718
- Date: March 13, 2023
- BST Products/Systems Referenced: S0 UAS
- Key Personnel: Jack Elston (PI)

## Executive Summary
Black Swift Technologies proposes to improve wildland firefighting safety by developing algorithms and data assimilation methods to generate automated UAS sampling patterns for gathering accurate wind and turbulence profiles in the lowest 5000 ft of atmosphere. BST will partner with NCAR/RAL and Colorado's Center of Excellence for Advanced Technology Aerial Firefighting to integrate advanced meteorological products into ATAK (Army Tactical Assault Kit), with field validation on 1-2 high-risk fire days using the S0 UAS equipped with meteorological sensors.

## Technical Approach
- Deploy teams of small, purpose-built UAS (S0) to make targeted observations of winds and turbulence
- Use advanced data assimilation methods developed at NCAR to improve forecasting
- Develop algorithms for automatically generating UAS sampling patterns based on current forecast models and observations
- Integrate meteorological products into existing wildland firefighting decision support tools (ATAK)
- Plan for future integration of wind/turbulence sensing capabilities onto other UAS and crewed aircraft
- Create sequential S0 flights for validation of forecasting improvements over 3-12 hour periods

## Products & Capabilities Described

### S0 UAS
- Small, purpose-built UAS designed for wildfire response operations
- Can be equipped with meteorological sensors for wind and turbulence measurement
- Capable of operating in hazardous environments with particulates and severe turbulence
- Intended for safe integration into airspace with manned aircraft through UTM-like systems

## Use Cases & Applications

### Primary Application
- **Wildland Firefighting**: Gathering low-level wind and turbulence data to improve safety of both airborne and surface-based firefighting assets; providing accurate 3D wind and turbulence profiles to inform tactical decisions

### Secondary Applications
- Volcano monitoring (hazardous particulate environments)
- Federal and commercial UTM applications
- NASA Earth Science applications including:
  - TCP (Tropospheric Composition Program)
  - Applied Sciences Air Quality Program
  - CALIPSO mission support
  - Aura mission support
  - CATS (Cloud-Aerosol Transport System)
  - OCO-3 (Orbiting Carbon Observatory 3)
  - Earth Ventures airborne field campaigns

## Technical Objectives & Specific Deliverables
1. Develop algorithms and methods for automatically generating UAS sampling patterns based on forecast models and observations
2. Create operational requirements, risk assessment, and mitigation documentation for operating S0 UAS in wildfire response
3. Gather meteorological data during 1-2 high-risk fire days from locations identified through data denial experiments
4. Demonstrate and quantify forecasting improvements for low-level wind fields over 3-12 hours post-sampling using sequential S0 flights

## Partnerships
- NCAR/RAL (National Center for Atmospheric Research/Research Applications Laboratory) - advanced data assimilation methods
- Colorado's Center of Excellence for Advanced Technology Aerial Firefighting

## Notable Details
- Critical gap identified: limited observations of winds and turbulence in lowest 5000 ft of atmosphere during wildfire operations
- Integration with existing tools (ATAK) rather than developing new platforms
- Focus on improving UTM safety for mixed manned/unmanned aircraft operations in wildfire airspace
- NASA Ames identified as primary customer with multiple other NASA Earth Science program applications
- Emphasis on hazardous environment capability (particulates, turbulence) as competitive advantage# Broad Area Announcement: Demonstration of Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (UAS) Payloads/Technology/Applications/Equipment

## Document Metadata
- **Type:** Broad Area Announcement (solicitation for vendor demonstrations)
- **Client/Agency:** U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, Preparedness Division
- **Program/Solicitation:** UAS Payloads/Technology/Applications/Equipment Demonstration
- **Date:** Not explicitly stated; event scheduled for early November 2024
- **BST Products/Systems Referenced:** None identified in this document
